record.title: Inherited Finland–Norway restriction on ordinary cross-border reindeer husbandry
record.scope: Finland–Norway land-frontier husbandry/grazing regime; treaty fence line is the operative divide where specified, with the international boundary operative between Angeli and boundary cairn 343.
record.crossings: Frontier grazing areas; not general passenger checkpoints
record.movement: Reindeer crossing the treaty-defined divide for ordinary husbandry/grazing, subject to designated-route and lawful slaughter-import exceptions.
record.exceptions: Articles 7–11 regulate recovery/return of strays. Article 19 permits commission-designated migration routes across the other state, without grazing during that movement, and excludes lawfully imported slaughter reindeer under secure guarding. Fence deviations mean the operative grazing divide is not everywhere the international line. No general passenger or all-livestock trade ban asserted.
record.imposing_authority: Norwegian and Finnish authorities under bilateral reindeer conventions
record.enforcement: Bilateral fences, owner guarding duties and regulated return of straying reindeer; legal policy and physical compliance are distinguished.
record.relationship: Promoted from R15-EU-L002. 2017 treaty renewal is not a newly dated closure.
record.status_observation: Agricultural authority page updated 13 September 2024 describes the exclusion; no 2026 cutoff extension inferred.
record.official_rationale: The Norwegian government’s treaty explanation states that the convention allocates responsibilities for fences and other measures to prevent reindeer crossing the Finland–Norway boundary and for handling incursions. This is a known husbandry and boundary-administration reason outside the current rationale taxonomy.
record.context: Historical seasonal grazing movement; fence coverage and legal prohibition have different timelines.
record.uncertainty: Historical effective onset unknown; 1852 declaration did not immediately end grazing, and January 1 2017 renews the treaty. The narrow legal husbandry regime is evidenced, not perfect physical enforcement, every commercial import condition, or a prohibition on the explicit treaty exceptions.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Authorities describe the inherited frontier husbandry exclusion; treaty scope and exceptions narrow this to the ordinary grazing/herding regime.
Inherited within window; 1852 declaration and later implementation stages do not justify precise onset.
No reopening established; no end imputed to observation cutoff.

Hierarchical coding review: Known reason outside taxonomy. The husbandry/boundary-administration objective is known but outside this taxonomy. No disease-control purpose is inferred from animal movement alone. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Administrative husbandry objective evidenced; six-code rationale left empty.

Ordinary husbandry/grazing across the treaty-defined divide, with explicit stray-return, commission-designated migration-route and lawful slaughter-import exceptions; fence deviations retained. Not a universal livestock or passenger prohibition.
Successive legal instruments and current authority account establish inherited regime, not unbroken observed enforcement.
